walkthroughs.body_html: Wind and solar generation depend on weather and time of day. To keep the grid stable, operators combine forecasting, geographic diversity, flexible gas plants, interconnectors with neighbours, demand response and storage. Pumped hydro and lithium-ion batteries can absorb surplus and discharge during shortfalls within seconds.

Lithium-ion batteries respond fast and suit short-duration smoothing but degrade over thousands of cycles. Pumped hydroelectric storage pumps water uphill when electricity is cheap and releases it through turbines when needed, with round-trip efficiency around 75 to 80 percent and lifetimes over 50 years.

Even renewables have embodied emissions from manufacturing turbines, panels and concrete foundations. Typical lifecycle gCO2 per kWh: coal around 820, gas 490, solar PV 40 to 50, wind 11 to 12, nuclear 12. Comparing lifecycle figures rather than direct emissions gives a fairer picture of climate impact.

options: Captures kinetic and potential energy of tides; predictable but site-limited.

Turbines convert kinetic energy of wind into electricity; offshore arrays are increasingly common.
Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight directly into electricity via the photoelectric effect.
